subject: psychology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: The study by Carmichael showing labels changed how people redrew shapes supports which idea?
options: That language can influence memory and thought
questions.explain: Carmichael found that verbal labels biased how figures were reproduced, supporting language's influence on thought.

questions.q: The nativist view (e.g. Chomsky) suggests humans are born with what?
questions.explain: Nativists argue humans have an innate, biological capacity that makes language acquisition possible.

questions.q: Reduced eye contact in conversation can communicate what?
options: Things such as discomfort or dishonesty
questions.explain: Eye contact is a non-verbal signal; reduced eye contact may signal discomfort, shyness or evasiveness.

questions.q: Von Frisch's research on honeybees showed they communicate the location of food using what?
questions.explain: Von Frisch found bees use a waggle dance to signal the direction and distance of food sources.

questions.q: 'Personal space' in non-verbal communication refers to what?
options: The distance we keep between ourselves and others
questions.explain: Personal space is the comfortable physical distance people keep between themselves and others.

questions.q: Piaget's view on language and thought is that what comes first?
questions.explain: Piaget argued that thought develops first and language reflects a child's existing level of thinking.

questions.q: Which of the following is a form of NON-VERBAL communication?
questions.explain: Body language is non-verbal communication, conveying meaning without words.

questions.q: Open, relaxed posture compared with crossed arms is an example of communication through what?
questions.explain: Posture is part of body language, a form of non-verbal communication that signals attitude and mood.

questions.q: Which is a recognised FUNCTION of language?
questions.explain: A core function of language is to communicate ideas, information and intentions between people.

questions.q: Standing very close to someone who wants more space is an example of breaking which non-verbal norm?
questions.explain: Standing too close violates personal-space norms, a key aspect of non-verbal communication.

questions.q: The Sapir-Whorf hypothesis (linguistic relativity) claims what?
options: Language influences the way we think
Thought has no link to language
questions.explain: The Sapir-Whorf hypothesis proposes that the language we speak shapes and influences how we think.

questions.q: Research suggesting the Inuit have many words for snow is used to discuss which hypothesis?
questions.explain: The 'words for snow' example is often cited (and debated) in relation to the Sapir-Whorf linguistic relativity hypothesis.
